$$k + a_1 + \cdots + a_m = a_1 a_2 \cdots a_m$$

$$\prod_{i=1}^m a_i - \sum_{i=1}^m (a_i - 1) = 2011. \tag{$\star$}$$

The sum we want to maximize equals the product $P = \prod a_i$, and $P = 2011 + \sum(a_i - 1)$, so maximizing $P$ is equivalent to maximizing $\sum(a_i - 1)$.

**Substitution.** Let $b_i = a_i - 1 \geq 1$. Then $(\star)$ becomes:

$$\prod_{i=1}^m (1+b_i) - \sum_{i=1}^m b_i = 2011.$$

$$\sum_{\substack{S \subseteq \{1,\ldots,m\} \\ |S| \geq 2}} \prod_{i \in S} b_i = 2010. \tag{$\star\star$}$$

We want to maximize $\sum b_i$ (equivalently, $P = 2011 + \sum b_i$).

Since all terms in $(\star\star)$ are non-negative, $\sum_{i<j} b_i b_j \leq 2010$, so:
